answer_1.quote: Given a new scenario name, our model ... can produce the entire schema ... Our model is extensible and can support new types of event-event relations ... We output a schema graph of event nodes and event-event relation edges, including temporal relations and hierarchical relations.
answer_1.outputs: Event schemas represented as graphs with textual event descriptions and temporal/hierarchical relations

answer_2.quote: For automatic evaluation of the schema quality against human-created schemas, we adopt Event F1 and Relation F1 metrics. Event F1 is similar to the Event Match metric ... We further define Relation F1 metrics for temporal relations and hierarchical relations respectively.

answer_4.quote: Human assessors are presented with the scenario name and a subgraph ... We then ask the assessor to write a coherent short story ... After they complete the story writing task, they will be asked to rate their experience from several aspects on a 5-point Likert scale.
answer_4.guideline: Assessors write a story based on a subgraph, then answer Likert-scale questions about coverage, usefulness of event names/descriptions, understandability, relevance, and overall helpfulness.
